newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia foreign reserves $9.89 bln at close '96.
newsitem.headline: Colombia foreign reserves $9.89 bln at close '96.

text.p: Colombia's net foreign reserves stood at $9.89 billion at the close of 1996, the central bank said in a report Monday.
The figure represents a 18.9 percent rise year-on-year. On Dec. 30, the final day's trade of 1996, net foreign reserves increased $411 million in just four hours.

The central bank had forecast net foreign reserves to increase by just $100 million through 1996. But as foreign investment flowed in, coupled with earnings from a wave of privatizations, net foreign reserves increased by $1.57 billion from $8.32 billion at the end of 1995.

Net reserves had already climbed by $543.2 million between Dec. 20 and Dec. 27. On the final day's trade of the year a record $474 million was pumped into foreign exchange markets and at the time traders said the central bank bought at least $400 million of that to prop up a weak dollar.

Colombia's strengthening peso has caused serious problems for exporters, who have seen the price competitiveness of their goods undermined by a strong peso in the international market place. The key coffee sector has also complained that the falling peso value of their exports has sent the cost of production skyrocketing.

At the start of last week, the government declared a state of economic emergency to combat a yawning fiscal deficit. The measures included sweeping measures to restrict public and private sector companies contracting new foreign debt. They also included plans to cut back the government's foreign debt program by $800 million.
